source_metadata.title: Cannabinoids for the treatment of dementia
source_metadata.source_type: Cochrane systematic review of randomized controlled trials

batch_manifest.scope: abstract, eligibility, methods, included-study overview, disclosures
review-level quantitative results and safety analyses

source_internal_inconsistencies: Cognition analysis population differs across source locations: abstract reports 28 participants, Summary of Findings reports 39, detailed Results reports 38; atom uses 38, the detailed analysis population.
Overall BPSD population differs: Summary of Findings reports 111 participants while detailed Results reports 110; atom uses 110.
Narrative p-values for CMAI, NPI agitation/aggression, weight, and CGI Change appear to conflate heterogeneity and overall-effect tests in places; atoms use the Data and Analyses forest-plot values.
The narrative contains an apparent typo of 502 participants for an euphoria adverse-event comparison; the Data and Analyses table shows 50.
The narrative and Data and Analyses table differ for the fatigue odds ratio; fatigue was not atomized separately.

extraction_limitations: LiteratureAtom is oriented to primary studies; this source is a systematic review. Review-level pooled estimates are tagged review_level_meta_analysis, and single-study findings are tagged secondary_reported_result.
Underlying trial results were not represented as if this review enrolled participants; primary-study atoms require direct extraction from the cited trial publications.
Bibliographic entries were excluded from atomization and handled separately as a task queue.
GRADE certainty and meta-analysis heterogeneity have no dedicated typed fields in schema v1.0 and are preserved in canonical statements, tags, and original result text where feasible.
schema_gaps: No typed source-design field for systematic reviews/meta-analyses.
No dedicated fields for GRADE certainty, heterogeneity statistics, or pooled-versus-single-study evidence status.
